items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: the trio record that I just released called “Soundscape” with my current trio of Ron Vincent and Dean Johnson

ctx.x: That’s a way to put it. I love the mystery of improvising. I’ve asked the question many times what are people thinking about, etcetera, and I think it’s sort of wonderful that there is no concrete answer.

Well it’s interesting because the trio record that I just released called “Soundscape” with my current trio of Ron Vincent and Dean Johnson and I wrote in my notes that people ask me sometimes what are you thinking about when you’re improvising and instead of the notes I’m thinking about nothing. I’m aware on a subliminal level of the arc, the form, the underlying harmonies of what I’m playing if I’m playing a structured piece as opposed to a free piece. But I’m not thinking G seven, A flat seven, it’s just all…

No, no. I love tangents. I’m wondering if you think joy has become something that the current generation of jazz musicians – how do I phrase this – seems less important than gravitas. I just got a letter from a former student who witnessed a jazz trio in a club in San Francisco I guess, and he just described it as if it was they were fighting to get something out to the audi – actually that they just were playing for themselves and it was like a competition, an athletic competition or something. I’m not…
